results.content:
Diffusion models (DMs). DMs generate data samples by iteratively denoising random noise. This sampling process inversely mirrors the forward data corruption mechanism: z_t = α_t z + σ_t ε where z = E(x) ~ q(z) with E representing a pretrained encoder and x the data variable. The noise term ε follows the prior distribution N(0, I). The transition kernel from time 0 to t is given by q_t(z_t|z) = N(z_t; α_t z, σ_t^2 I). The training objective [12] is as follows:
L_DM(φ) = E_{q(t) q(z,c) N(ε;0,I)}[||ε − ε_φ(z_t, t, c)||_2^2], (1)
where q(t): time sampling distribution, and q(z, c): joint distribution of latent z and condition c.
results.route_rationale: Standard denoising training objective — a definition of the loss; asserts no non-trivial property and is not a formalisable non-trivial claim.
results.reasoning: Equation (1) is the standard DDPM/flow-matching denoising objective: an expectation, over t ~ q(t), (z,c) ~ q(z,c) and ε ~ N(0,I), of the squared L2 error between the target noise ε and the model prediction ε_φ(z_t, t, c). It is a definition (loss objective), not a derivation step, and is well-formed given z_t = α_t z + σ_t ε. No algebraic or logical step is asserted that could be wrong.

results.content:
Given a pretrained operator f_ϕ^l at layer l, we learn a new operator g_θ^l that approximates f_ϕ^l [17]. Since DiT activations are continuous and smooth, this can be posed as a regression problem:
L(θ) = E_{q(t) q(z) q_t(z_t | z)} [ ||g_θ^l(z_t, t) - f_ϕ^l(z_t, t)||_p^p ] where p ∈ {1, 2} and the conditioning c is implicitly absorbed into the latent representation z through a learned embedding ψ(c), though we omit ψ for notational simplicity. Note that L_reg(·,·) = ||·||_p^p when using L_p norms. (2)
results.route_rationale: Activation-distillation regression objective — a definition; nothing formalisable/non-trivial to prove.
results.reasoning: Equation (2) defines the activation-distillation regression objective: the expected L_p norm (p ∈ {1, 2}) between the new operator output g_θ^l(z_t, t) and the pretrained operator output f_ϕ^l(z_t, t). The surrounding text states that conditioning c is absorbed into z (hence q(z) rather than q(z,c) inside the expectation) — an explained notational choice, not an error. The equation is well-formed; there is no derivation to go wrong.

results.content:
Given an attention matrix A ∈ R^{N×N} and a band size of k, we define a bi-directional band indicator matrix B_k ∈ R^{N×N} as:
(B_k)_{i,j} = { 1, if |i − j| ≤ k
                0, otherwise }
Then, locality within a band of size k is computed as:
L_k = (1/N) ∑_{i,j} A_{i,j} (B_k)_{i,j} (3)
results.route_rationale: Definition of the band-k locality metric; the only checkable content is well-formedness. The empirical claim (L_k > 0.7 for all layers at k=32) is data-dependent and unformalisable.
results.reasoning: B_k is a {0,1} indicator of |i − j| ≤ k, and L_k = (1/N) Σ_{i,j} A_{i,j} (B_k)_{i,j}. For an attention matrix A with non-negative entries and rows summing to 1, Σ_{i,j} A_{i,j} = N, and since 0 ≤ B_k ≤ 1 pointwise, 0 ≤ L_k ≤ 1. This matches the paper's reading of L_k as the fraction of attention mass inside a band of width k. The definition is internally consistent.

results.location: G Hyena-X and Hyena-Y operators: Additional details
results.route_rationale: Operator definition — checkable for index/dimension consistency by inspection; formalising a pure definition in Lean would add no proof obligation.
results.reasoning: Dimensional and index consistency: x ∈ R^{ℓ×d}; W, U, P, M ∈ R^{d×d} mix the channel index c; T, H, K, G ∈ R^{ℓ×ℓ} mix the position index s; hence q, k, v, y ∈ R^{ℓ×d}. The final line y_s^c = Σ_{c'} q_s^{c'} (Σ_{s'} G_{ss'}^{c'} k_{s'}^{c'}) v_s^{c'} M^{c'c} is the gated pointwise product q ⊙ (Gk) ⊙ v mixed over channels by M — the standard Hyena structure. Setting G = I makes the bracket equal to k_s^{c'} (Hyena-X removes the implicit convolution); removing T, H, K leaves q = xW, k = xU, v = xP (Hyena-Y keeps only the short explicit G convolution). All four equations are mutually consistent.

results.content:
• Input projections (Q, K, V): 6LD^2
• Softmax attention: 2L^2D + HL^2 (note: we use an optimized kernel that reduces FLOPs by 50%)
• Output projection: 2LD^2
• Total: 8LD^2 + 2L^2D + HL^2
results.route_rationale: FLOP cost-model arithmetic; the only checkable identity is Total = sum of the three components, which is trivial ring arithmetic.
results.reasoning: The components sum exactly to the stated total: 6LD^2 + 2L^2D + HL^2 + 2LD^2 = 8LD^2 + 2L^2D + HL^2. QKV input projections (6LD^2 = 3 × 2LD^2) and the output projection (2LD^2) follow the standard 2LD^2-per-linear-map convention. The softmax-attention term 2L^2D + HL^2 is a stated cost-model convention (with the noted 50% optimized-kernel reduction); it contains the quadratic-in-L terms 2L^2D and HL^2, consistent with the paper's claim that MHA scales quadratically with sequence length. No arithmetic error.

results.content:
• Input projections (Q, K, V): 6LD^2
• Sliding window attention (bidirectional): 4L(2w + 1)D + 2HL(2w + 1)
• Output projection: 2LD^2
results.route_rationale: FLOP cost-model arithmetic; checkable by inspection.
results.reasoning: A bidirectional sliding window of size w gives 2w+1 attended positions per query: QK^T costs 2L(2w+1)D and attention·V costs 2L(2w+1)D, summing to 4L(2w+1)D; 2HL(2w+1) is a per-head softmax term analogous to the HL^2 term in the MHA model. Internally consistent with the MHA counting convention.

• Input projections: 6LD^2

• Inner filter convolution: LDK × 2
• Gates: LD × 2
• Output projection: 2LD^2
results.route_rationale: FLOP cost-model arithmetic; checkable by inspection.
results.reasoning: Three featurizer convolutions (q, k, v) at 2LDK each give 3LDK × 2, an inner filter convolution at LDK × 2, gates at LD × 2, plus the shared projection convention (6LD^2 input + 2LD^2 output). Consistent with the Hyena-SE operator structure (featurizer plus inner filter both present). No total is asserted, so there is nothing further to contradict.

The expression is internally consistent as a cost model; no arithmetic identity is asserted that could be contradicted.

results.location: 6 Case Study: Converting Model Depth to Width via Grafting / Table 6
results.content: A.R. (Aspect Ratio) is defined as model width divided by depth (e.g., 1152/14 = 82.3). — Table 6 A.R. column: DiT-L/2 42.7; U-ViT-L 48.8; DiT-B/2 64.0; BK-SDM 82.3; TinyDiT-D14 82.3; TinyDiT-D14 w/ MKD 82.3; DiT-XL/2 41.4; Grafting (Ours) 164.6.
results.route_rationale: Aspect-Ratio definition with worked arithmetic examples; every value is a deterministic width/depth ratio, so each is checkable by inspection.
results.reasoning: A.R. is defined as width/depth. The caption's worked example 1152/14 = 82.3 is correct (82.2857… rounds to 82.3). Checking the paper's own computations: DiT-L/2: 1024/24 = 42.67 → 42.7 ✓; DiT-B/2: 768/12 = 64.0 ✓; U-ViT-L: 1024/21 = 48.76 → 48.8 ✓; Grafting: 2304/14 = 164.57 → 164.6 ✓. But DiT-XL/2 has width 1152 and depth 28, so 1152/28 = 41.142857…, which rounds to 41.1 at one decimal place, yet Table 6 reports 41.4. The value 41.4 would require width 41.4 × 28 = 1159.2, contradicting the stated width 1152. This is an arithmetic/rounding error confined to the table value.

findings.evidence: Table 6 reports A.R. = 41.4 for DiT-XL/2. Under the paper's own definition (A.R. = width/depth) with DiT-XL/2's config (width 1152, depth 28), A.R. = 1152/28 = 41.142857…, which rounds to **41.1**, not 41.4; 41.4 would require width 1159.2. The caption's own example (1152/14 = 82.3) and the other computed rows (DiT-L/2: 1024/24 = 42.7; DiT-B/2: 768/12 = 64.0; U-ViT-L: 1024/21 = 48.8; Grafting: 2304/14 = 164.6) all round correctly.

summary: Verified the mathematics of 5217 (Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting), an empirical ML paper containing no theorems, lemmas, or proofs. Twelve self-contained mathematical objects were extracted: the two loss/objective definitions (Eqs. 1–2), the band-k locality metric (Eq. 3), the four Hyena operator equations (App. G), the seven FLOP cost-model formulas (App. H), and the Aspect-Ratio definition (Table 6). All twelve are definitions or inspection-level arithmetic — none is a formalisable non-trivial claim whose correctness turns on a real argument — so every snippet routed to informal verify-math and the Lean queue was empty (N = 0); no Lean project was created for this paper, and the pre-existing sibling project MATH_VERIFICATION/Paper was left untouched. All definitions and cost models checked out, including the MHA FLOP total identity (6LD² + 2L²D + HL² + 2LD² = 8LD² + 2L²D + HL²) and the L_k ∈ [0,1] property implied by the locality metric. One minor arithmetic error was found: Table 6 reports A.R. = 41.4 for DiT-XL/2, but width/depth = 1152/28 = 41.142857…, which rounds to 41.1. The error is confined to a table value and does not invalidate any main claim. No Lean FAILED results were produced, so no informal fallbacks were required.
